objective: Complete exploration breadth and test whether recent CPSC recall records contain stable structured identifiers.
actions: Added and scored candidates in transit accessibility and federal rulemaking
Fetched the official CPSC recall API and profiled the first 100 returned records
Revised the recall-screening mechanism and score based on measured identifier coverage
Recorded five evidence entries with incumbent alternatives and limitations
hypothesis: Recent CPSC recall notices expose structured model or UPC identifiers often enough for direct item matching.
checks: Parsed 9,891 records from the official CPSC JSON endpoint and calculated the stated metrics on the first 100
Confirmed five actual candidates span five materially different domains
Checked every new candidate includes an incumbent alternative and falsification argument
limitations: The CPSC profile is a recent convenience sample, not a random or population sample
No user interviews, accounts, outreach, or external transactions were performed
Transit API completeness and incumbent alert usability were not directly tested
Candidate scores remain provisional judgments rather than measured user outcomes
next: Shortlist at most three candidates and compare each proposed output against the official workflow on real records.
